close_reason: Implemented in commit 592c7af. Added a one-paragraph rustdoc note on the merge_extras helper stating the expected extras size is zero (common case) or single-digit, per-key hash lookup is O(1) average, no allocation budget concern in practice, with a pointer to build_request for callers who actually need hundreds of extras.
description: src/methods/metadata.rs:102-107: iterates p.extra (owned), calling args.as_object_mut().expect(...).entry(k).or_insert(v) per key. Each iteration unwraps the args mutable object reference, does a hash lookup, and inserts. Vendor-extras maps in production are typically tiny (<10 keys); this is fine in practice. Worth a one-line comment noting the expected size to head off well-intentioned 'optimization' PRs. No code change required if the comment is added. Demonstrated impact at scale: none. Listed only because Section 2 protocol requires non-trivial allocation paths be examined; conclusion is 'fine, document it'.
title: metadata_changes extras-loop: per-key Map::entry/or_insert with no documented allocation budget
